Generative Bionics is an Italian company founded on research and technologies developed at the Italian Institute of Technology (IIT) and dedicated to building intelligent humanoid robots based on Physical AI. The company integrates robotics, artificial intelligence, and design to develop humanoids designed to operate safely and reliably in real-world settings, prioritizing industrial use cases.

Generative Bionics is a startup founded based on research results from the Italian Institute of Technology (IIT). CEO Daniele Pucci is a figure who has led world-renowned humanoid research for many years, including the cognitive robot 'iCub', the industrial collaborative robot 'ergoCub', and the jet-propelled flying 'iRonCub', and Generative Bionics was born as an extension of that research.

GENE.01 is a humanoid platform with a body that has become a sensory organ, completed by Pucci and his team in just six months. The keyword the company promotes is 'Human-centric Physical AI'. The foundation is the philosophy of creating robots that humans can naturally accept, rather than forcing humans to adapt to robots.

In many humanoid developments, the basic flow is 'see with a camera,' 'AI makes a decision,' and 'move the body.' This is an approach that advances intelligence with vision as the axis. In contrast, Generative Bionics advocates the concept of 'Body as Compute,' treating the body itself as part of the computer.

At 'AMD Advancing AI' hosted by AMD, a demo was shown where CEO Lisa Su herself shook hands with GENE.01. The robot sensed her approaching and recognized her presence even before contact. This is due to the company's unique mechanism that combines proximity sensors, tactile sensors, and a VLA (Vision-Language-Action) model.

For humanoids working in the same space as people, 'not bumping into things,' 'not surprising people,' and 'reacting naturally' are important conditions. GENE.01 is designed with the goal of meeting these conditions.

AMD is an investor in Generative Bionics and also a technical partner that jointly builds the robot's computing foundation, including CPUs, GPUs, FPGAs, and embedded vision. Pucci explains that they 'treat the body as part of computing,' and AMD is in a position to provide the computing foundation that supports that massive real-time processing.
A 'platform,' not a finished product

Generative Bionics is not thinking about selling GENE.01 as a single finished product. They have a vision of cultivating it as a platform where researchers and companies can develop industrial robots on the same foundation by releasing open libraries and digital twins. They say the intended use extends beyond factories to medical care and healthcare.

Concrete industrial applications are already underway. Through a collaboration with Fincantieri, a company known globally in the shipbuilding sector, they are in the process of developing work at shipyards as their first industrial use case.

The company is also working on research into wearable devices that extend human capabilities, not limited to humanoids. A smart helmet equipped with 'Surround Vision' to compensate for blind spots is introduced as one example. The company's philosophy of fusing humans and machines is spreading to areas other than robots.
